title: Deck Removal Cost in Hampton Roads: Prices, Permits, and What's Included

contentHtml:
Deck removal typically costs $1,000 to $7,000 or more, according to HomeGuide's 2026 deck removal cost guide. A small, low deck sits at the bottom of that range. A large, raised or multi-level deck with concrete footings sits at the top.

This guide explains what drives the price, what a full removal should include, which permits and old-lumber rules apply in Hampton Roads, and how to get a quote you can compare.

Deck removal cost by size

National averages from HomeGuide:

Deck sizeTypical national cost
Small (100 to 200 sq ft)$1,000 to $2,500
Medium (200 to 400 sq ft)$2,500 to $5,000
Large (400+ sq ft)$5,000 to $7,000+

Use these as a starting point, not a local quote. Hampton Roads labor and disposal rates differ from national averages. Mr Demo Pro quotes deck removal per project after reviewing the deck's size, height and how it attaches to the house. Estimates are free.

What changes the price

  • Size: more square feet means more boards, joists and debris to haul.

  • Height and levels: raised and multi-level decks need more care, staging and labor than a deck a step off the ground.

  • Attachment to the house: a deck bolted to the house through a ledger board has to be detached without damaging siding or brick.

  • Footings: posts set in concrete take longer to pull than posts on surface blocks.

  • Extras: stairs, railings, built-in benches, pergolas and skirting add material and time.

  • Material and disposal: wood and composite are heavy, and disposal is charged by weight. Ask whether haul-off is in the price. HomeGuide notes that some companies charge extra for treated wood.

  • Access: a backyard reached through a narrow gate means longer carries to the truck.

What a full deck removal includes

A low quote sometimes covers only tearing off the boards. A complete job leaves the yard ready for what comes next. Mr Demo Pro's deck removal service follows four steps:

  1. Inspection. The crew checks the deck's condition and plans the safest way to take it apart.

  2. Dismantling. Boards, railings and structural framing come off piece by piece, and attached decks are detached carefully from the house.

  3. Foundation removal. Posts, footings and remaining structural pieces come out of the ground.

  4. Final cleanup. All debris, nails and hardware are hauled away, and post holes are filled.

When you compare quotes, check each one for footing removal, haul-off and hole filling. Those three items explain most of the gap between a cheap number and a complete one.

Do you need a permit to remove a deck?

It depends on the city and the deck. The City of Virginia Beach lists decks among the structures that need a residential building permit and states that the demolition or removal of a structure also requires a permit. Rules differ across Norfolk, Chesapeake, Hampton, Newport News, Portsmouth and Suffolk, so check with your city's building department before work starts. An attached deck, a raised deck or a deck with wiring is the most likely to need one.

Older decks: treated lumber and lead paint

Arsenic-treated lumber in pre-2004 decks

According to the EPA, decks built before 2004 were often made with wood treated with chromated copper arsenate (CCA). Manufacturers stopped making it for homeowner use in December 2003. The EPA advises never burning CCA or other treated wood, wearing goggles and a dust mask when cutting it, and not reusing it as mulch. State and local disposal rules can be stricter, which is one reason haul-off belongs in the quote.

Lead paint on pre-1978 homes

If the deck is attached to a home built before 1978, removing it can disturb painted siding or trim. The EPA's lead renovation rule applies when paid work on a pre-1978 home disturbs more than 20 square feet of exterior painted surface, and it requires lead-safe work practices.

Removing a deck and fence together

Many backyard projects clear more than one structure. If an old fence, shed or concrete pad is coming out too, ask for everything on the same estimate so one crew can plan the whole job.

How to get an accurate deck removal quote

Have these details ready when you call:

  • Rough size in feet, or the number of boards across and down

  • Height off the ground and the number of levels

  • Whether the deck is attached to the house

  • Stairs, railings, built-ins or wiring

  • How the posts are set, if you know: concrete, blocks or buried

  • Gate width and any access limits

DIY or hire a pro?

A small, low, freestanding deck is a manageable project for a handy homeowner with a truck and a disposal plan. Raised, attached or concrete-footed decks are harder and riskier. Our DIY vs. pro demolition guide covers the trade-offs.

Deck removal FAQ

How much does deck removal cost in Hampton Roads?

National averages run from about $1,000 for a small deck to $7,000 or more for a large one. Mr Demo Pro provides a free quote after reviewing your deck's size, height and attachment.

Do I need a permit to remove a deck?

Sometimes. Virginia Beach requires a permit to demolish or remove a structure. Check with your city's building department, especially for attached or raised decks.

Can you remove an attached deck without damaging the house?

Yes. The deck is detached from the house carefully to protect siding, brick and the ledger area.

What happens to the debris?

Mr Demo Pro hauls away all boards, framing, posts and hardware as part of the job, so you do not need a dumpster.

Are the posts and footings removed?

Yes. Posts, footings and remaining structural pieces come out, and the holes are filled.

Mr Demo Pro serves homeowners across Hampton Roads. Tell us about your deck, and we will give you a free quote. Call 757-848-4559 or request a free quote online.
